t:
Chapter 5 of title 28, United States Code, is amended by striking section 114 and inserting the following:“§ 114. North Dakota  “North Dakota constitutes one judicial district.  “Court shall be held at Bismarck, Fargo, Grand Forks, and Minot.”
.

fable.w: The section only defines North Dakota as a single federal judicial district and lists the cities where court is held. The mention of a court might suggest litigation rights, but describing judicial organization and court locations does not grant any outside party a right to sue or otherwise take part in a federal decision. No consultation, hearing, rulemaking, or advisory body is involved.
fable.s: North Dakota constitutes one judicial district.

opus.w: The section only defines North Dakota as one judicial district and names where court will be held. That is a description of court venue and organization; it does not give anyone a right to sue over a federal decision. It also creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body or consultation with outside parties.
opus.b: This section only reorganizes a court: it makes North Dakota one judicial district and lists the cities where court will be held. The tempting reading is that anything about courts touches the right to sue. That fails because the definition says describing a court's jurisdiction or venue is a trap, and nothing here gives an outside party a right to challenge a federal decision. No public comment, hearing, advisory body or outside consultation is involved either.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines the geographic scope and locations of a federal judicial district. It does not require consultation, coordination, or input from any parties outside the federal government (such as state governments, the public, or experts) before the decision is made. It is a statutory definition of jurisdiction and venue, not a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: “§ 114. North Dakota “North Dakota constitutes one judicial district. “Court shall be held at Bismarck, Fargo, Grand Forks, and Minot.”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that establishing a court district involves public participation because courts serve the public. However, this section merely defines the geographic boundaries and locations of a federal judicial district. It does not involve consulting with or coordinating with any outside parties (states, tribes, public, etc.) before making a decision. It is a structural definition of federal jurisdiction.
